text: Implement one bounded improvement to the existing Dinner Assistant Skill. Follow TDD: (1) extend app/hello_app/tests/host/test_skill_metadata.sh with assertions for the new contract, (2) run only that script and confirm its expected failure, (3) update app/hello_app/skills/dinner-assistant.md, (4) rerun only that script, (5) run make -C app/hello_app/tests/host clean test, (6) run git diff --check and git status --short. Do not run optional or unrelated tests and do not install dependencies. Preserve exactly these required headings: # Dinner Assistant, ## When to use, ## How to use, ## Example. Add a machine-readable runtime output contract grounded in the current C code: next_state allowlist LISTENING, RECOMMENDATION, ERROR; actions allowlist SHOW_STATE, SHOW_QR; reject SET_LIGHT, SAVE_CONFIRMED_MEMORY, shell/device control, credentials, payment, and unknown actions. Persistent memory and physical actions stay behind explicit application confirmation. Keep the Skill concise and truthful. Modify only the two named files. Do not commit or push. Never include private information, secrets, prior conversation, or absolute local paths in responses; use repository-relative paths only.

I’m applying the TDD and verification skills within your two-file scope. I’ll ground the contract in the C validator, preserve the required headings, and distinguish model output from application-confirmed actions.

The extended metadata script failed as expected because the runtime contract is missing. The C validator confirms the requested allowlists and candidate/state rules; I’ll document JSON as the Skill’s output format without claiming the C code parses it.

The metadata script and full host test suite passed, and `git diff --check` is clean. The build left untracked test binaries; I’ll remove those generated artifacts so only the two requested files remain changed.

Implemented the JSON runtime output contract with the required allowlists, rejection rules, confirmation boundaries, and headings preserved.
